Geyer1994Constrained supplies tangent-cone asymptotics for constrained M-estimators, not the branch-labelled causal random closed-set limit.

novelty_flags.label: Project-level survey / Theorems 1–3
novelty_flags.one_line: The survey omits Strieder and Drton (2024), Dual Likelihood for Causal Inference under Structure Uncertainty, a closer published single-environment structural-uncertainty/test-inversion comparator with a covariance-union formulation and closed-form confidence construction.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 3 — boundary random-set limit
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Tangent-cone regularity and C1 extension of every accessible branch map are assumed, not established for every LDiffPC fiber boundary.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The boundary random-set limit is claimed conditionally on tangent-cone regularity and branch smoothness at the specified s0.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Diff-faithfulness equates regression-coefficient equality with diff-separation, and Theorem 1 gives the true difference-DAG skeleton with only correct output orientations under perfect equality information.
Theorem 4.1 gives an asymptotic confidence set for a total effect under unknown equal-variance Gaussian DAG structure, and Theorem 4.5 gives a finite-sample split-likelihood confidence set.

For Gaussian FCI, the paper gives exact finite-sample coverage with known outcome variance for the selected adjustment functional under its Markov-blanket condition, while structural-effect coverage is asymptotic up to a stated distortion.

The paper constructs unions of graph-specific estimates and confidence sets after resampling/screening PC discovery and proves asymptotically correct coverage for a fixed population-level causal effect.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 120(550), 2025
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work protects inference after randomized/differentially-private causal discovery by a miscoverage-level correction; it is not a paired completion-fiber procedure.
The paper treats identification of total and direct causal changes and effects from difference graphs, but its published scope is causal reasoning rather than post-discovery confidence-set inference.
DCI estimates a two-environment shared-topological-order difference DAG using regression-coefficient invariance for skeleton recovery and residual-variance invariance for some orientations.

The paper develops test-inverted, structure-uncertainty confidence regions for a single-environment equal-error-variance Gaussian total effect and provides a closed-form dual-likelihood construction; it is a missed close comparator, though it does not subsume the paired LDiffPC boundary problem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add StriederDrton2024DualLikelihood to related work and state a strict comparison: its single-environment equal-variance total-effect test inversion versus the proposed two-environment equality-ledger direct-effect fiber, including why its closed-form dual construction cannot deliver the claimed boundary random-set law.

Promote the boundary theorem into the clear field kernel by adding a concrete, computable p=3 or p=4 branch-boundary corollary that evaluates the accessible cones, K^(0), and K^(1), and contrasts their expected diameter with the regular Wald limit.

Turn the noncontraction result from a witness calibration into a stronger efficiency statement by deriving a local expected-diameter lower bound for the same tangent experiment and comparing it directly with the confidence union’s local risk.

recommended_next_step: Revise the literature map and theorem gaps to incorporate the 2024 dual-likelihood structural-uncertainty result, then resubmit this field-tier angle for novelty review.
